knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The safe state is confirmed first: the manufacturer's method releases the pressure, and the machine is checked before any disconnection. Dragging the hose, disconnecting while pressurised and using a spare fitting are all unsafe or unauthorised.
A bulge is a defect under the Safe Work Australia jetting guide. The hose is tagged out, logged and reported. Taping, cutting and rejoining, or using it again, all keep a defective item in service.

An unidentified product is not used or decanted. The product is identified from its supplier record and safety data sheet first. Using a product by its colour or pouring it into an unlabelled bottle breaks the labelling and storage rules in this lesson.

practicalCriteria: On a supervised, de-energised demonstration unit or a paper site plan, the learner identifies each step of the manufacturer's shutdown sequence in order and names the check that confirms a safe state before disconnection.

On a supervised demonstration hose and fitting, the learner completes a visual inspection, identifies at least one defect, tags the item as defective and completes a defect log entry without repairing it.
The learner states, for a simulated chemical container with a worn label, why it is not used or decanted until the product is identified from its safety data sheet.
passRule: Assessor observes every practical criterion and records it as met or not met. The knowledge checks are not a practical pass. The minimum knowledge score is 80%, so all three checks must be correct.
evidenceRequired: Completed shutdown checklist for the demonstration unit
Defect log entry and tag for the demonstration hose or fitting
Assessor observation record for each practical criterion
stopWorkCriteria: A coupling is opened or a hose is disconnected while pressure remains
A defective hose or fitting is returned to use without a recorded test
Work above ground level is attempted without the licence or the written employer authorisation the task requires
